feature: any admin-only surface (an API route handler, or a server-rendered admin page/layout) that is expected to require an authenticated admin session on the server but does not call the shared auth check
symptom: an admin surface is added by a route or path that looks admin-only (it lives under an admin URL prefix, its UI hides itself from a normal reader) without going through the shared server-side auth wrapper/check. Because the surface never calls the check, nothing 401s an unauthenticated request -- the page or route just runs. The static shape recurs because the auth requirement lives in a convention ("every admin handler calls withAdminAuth() / checks the session"), not in something the framework enforces by default for a new file added under the admin path. Not written with route-level exploit detail here per the owner's public-repo rule -- see the linked fix PRs and the project rule for the mechanism.
first_seen: 2026-09-24, IPODhan: the Tier A review of PR #989 found 6 of 31 `web/app/api/admin/**/route.ts` handlers called no admin-auth helper and `web/middleware.ts` did not guard `/api/admin`; fixed on `main`, prod deploy deferred by owner decision (2026-09-24) to the next release. Recurrence 2026-09-29/30 (#1322): one SERVER-RENDERED admin page (not an API route) did not check the session on the server -- the same class in a different surface type, found after the API-route instance had already been fixed and the shared `withAdminAuth()` wrapper (`.claude/rules/admin-route-auth.md`) existed as the documented convention.
fix_prs: 2026-09-24 instance: fix branch `fix/admin-route-auth`, merged to main (prod deploy deferred, tracked as part of the OD-133/OD-135 release gate). #1322 instance: #1324 adds a static test asserting the page performs its own server-side session check; #1325 hardens the detector that would have caught #1322 before merge.
detection_check: partially guarded: #1324's static test covers the specific page fixed in #1322; #1325 hardens the detector for the class going forward. No single CI check yet enumerates every admin surface (API routes under web/app/api/admin/** AND server-rendered pages under the admin UI tree) and asserts each one calls the shared auth check -- the 2026-09-24 fix covered only the API-route half of the surface, which is why the 2026-09-29 recurrence landed on the page half instead.
